I also use cruise control (usually 5 to 10 below speed limit when not on the highway; whatever is slightly below traffic speed on the highway) and coast to red lights instead of slamming on the brakes.

For heavy use light fixtures, I have replaced them with LEDs but that saving isn't as noticeable. I found if I spend more on initial purchase that I replace those items far less. The LEDs are a good example, I have 3 flood lights in the main room of my apartment. When I wasn't using LED lights, I was replacing all 3 bulbs 2-3 times a year, while the LED last 3-5 years.

Focus on the big things if you want big results. Cutting coffee costs is cool, but not as impactful as cutting other expenses. Your home and car are probably your biggest expenses, so they'll offer the biggest opportunities to save.

  • Buying a modest size house instead of an average-or-bigger house will save you thousands of dollars every year between the sticker price, utilities, insurance, and taxes.

  • Optimize house location for driving distance for your frequent destinations (e.g. work). Driving is expensive. My commute is about 3 miles, and it's very doable by bike. Instead of driving 15,000 miles per year, I'm closer to 2,000. At $0.30 cents per mile that's $3900 per year.

  • Don't buy a fancy or stupidly large car (obvious exception: sensible truck/van for work if you haul shit around for your job regularly). Buying used cars instead of new cars, and buying less frequently, will save thousands of dollars every year between the lower upfront cost, and maybe better gas milage and insurance rates.

Once you have a lot of money invested, DIY investment management with proper funds will save thousands of dollars every year on management and fund fees (and probably outperform what a sketchy "professional" would do while extracting money from you). My barely-comfortably-retired parents would easily have twice as much saved up if they had just owned an index fund instead of the crap that was sold to them by investment professionals over the decades.
